Past analyses of AAPL (most recent first):

[2026-10-02 | AAPL | Overweight | +0.9% | -0.3% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Overweight

**Executive Summary**: Overweight AAPL — build gradually, do not chase at 333.69. Tranche 1 at roughly one-sixth to one-quarter of a standard full AAPL allocation, worked with limit orders inside 330.60–331.90 (Bollinger mid 331.90 / 10-1–10-2 lows), with the tranche's notional capped independently at ~10–12% of portfolio rather than the 20–25% the trader allowed — the −8.58% 7/31 gap proves the 325.80 stop is a level, not an exit, and a 20–25% notional tranche would risk ~1.7–2.1% of the portfolio on a repeat. Treat 325.80 as a closing-basis stop, halve the tranche on a close below 328.70, and treat a close below the 50-SMA at 322.42 as hard invalidation of the whole Overweight. If the limit zone goes unfilled for roughly five sessions while price holds above 331.90, fill half of Tranche 1 at market rather than forfeiting participation — the desk's repeated error is gating adds below a rising tape. Add Tranche 2 only on a daily close above 335.30 with volume above ~42.2M (ideally a held retest of 333–334), and Tranche 3 on whichever comes first: a held retest of 322.42 or a close above 341.07 with the MACD histogram turning positive. Trim back toward benchmark weight into 345.34; if that breaks on volume, hold the excess and trail with the 50-SMA. Horizon 1–3 months, re-underwritten at the late-October FQ4 FY2026 print.

**Investment Thesis**: The direction belongs to the bull; the entry and the size belong to the bear. That split is Overweight — not Buy, and not Hold.

WHAT THE BULL WON, AND NOBODY REFUTED. Direction first: the 200-SMA at 289.159 and the 50-SMA at 322.416 are both rising every session, price is 15.4% above the 200-SMA and 3.5% above the 50-SMA, and the 50/200 spread is widening to ~+11.5%. The conservative analyst's own words concede this — he calls AAPL "still a rising 50/200-SMA structure," names 322.42 as support and 345.34 as the resistance to trim into. The primary trend was not genuinely contested. The failed breakdown at 325.81 (undercut, then close at 330.32) followed by the 10/2 gap-and-hold to 333.69 has repaired the entire −8.58% July gap (7/30 pre-gap close 333.43, latest close 333.69 — within 26 cents, through the gap-fill line at 333.43). MACD at 3.807 is still above zero, RSI 54.72 is neutral, and RSI cooling ~12 points on a ~1.8% price decline is consolidation, not distribution. And the fundamental engine is accelerating, not bending: 9M FY2026 revenue +16.1% to $364.4B, Q3 revenue +16.4%, 9M diluted EPS +22.4%, Q3 EPS +28.7%, Q3 gross margin 50.1% (+357 bps) with cost of goods up only +11.2%, 9M operating margin +263 bps, 9M FCF $110.2B at a 30.2% margin, net cash $62.2B after $73.9B of returns. The bear called this "a phenomenal company" and then argued the tape — that is a timing and valuation case, not a thesis failure.

WHAT THE BEAR WON, AND WHY IT GOVERNS THE ENTRY. The near-term geometry is genuinely poor and the conservative and neutral seats documented it with levels, not adjectives: close at 333.69 pinned to the 10-EMA at 333.698, four consecutive sessions below the 10-EMA, 0.48% below the overhead VWMA at 335.30, lower highs 345.34 → 342.99 → 339.50 → 334.54, MACD below its 4.820 signal after seven down sessions from 6.248 with a negative histogram at −1.013, and a rebound on 33.28M shares versus a ~42.2M 20-day average (~21% light). The bull's own plan requires a 335.30 volume reclaim to confirm — so buying full size before that is internally inconsistent. The stop geometry is the decisive point both non-aggressive seats nailed: 5.45 points from 331.25 to 325.80 is only ~0.8 ATR (7.035), inside ordinary noise, and the trader never resolved whether 325.80 is intraday or closing-only. If intraday, expect whipsaw; if closing-only, the real maximum loss is larger than advertised. And the conservative's arithmetic on gap risk is the one argument the aggressive never answered: a 20–25% notional tranche through a −8.58%-style gap is 1.7–2.1% of portfolio, not 0.15–0.25%. The bull's 2.6:1 to the 345.34 high is a distance ratio, not an expected value, and it assumes the target prints before the stop.

WHY OVERWEIGHT AND NOT HOLD. The conservative's Hold/Wait is the weakest position in the debate because it is a directional call in disguise and it has no catalyst behind it. No seat produced a confirmed negative event: the AI/agent risk, App Store regulation and margin normalization are risks, not events. The inventory build (+94% total, +260% raw materials, finished goods −4.1%, ~17 days) is at least as consistent with a product-cycle pre-build as with demand failure — the bear's read requires the worst-case interpretation as much as the bull's requires the best. The "only hard news is a price-target cut" point is unverifiable noise: no analyst, rating, prior target or new target is disclosed, and the "$355" reference contradicts the "cut" framing; the "new CEO memo" item is uncorroborated. Missing information (no sentiment report) is not bearish information. Most importantly, this desk's own record is emphatic: Underweights and confirmation-gated Holds inside intact AAPL uptrends (07-13, 07-20–07-24, 08-11–08-13, 08-17, 08-21, 08-24, 08-27–08-28, 09-02, 09-08) repeatedly forfeited alpha while the Overweights paid, and the 09-14, 09-16 and 09-18 reflections all name the same execution error — tranches placed 2–3% below a rising tape that never fill, so the plan earns nothing from its own correct call. Sitting flat in a 16% grower with 50.1% gross margin and a stacked 50/200 structure, with no confirmed negative catalyst, is the bet that has cost this book the most.

WHY OVERWEIGHT AND NOT BUY. The trader sized for conviction the entry does not support. The neutral's structural correction is adopted because both colleagues' objections to it are valid: cut the starter to ~1/6–1/4 of standard allocation with the notional capped at ~10–12% of portfolio, size explicitly for a gap toward 322.42 and then 317.17, and state that 325.80 is a closing-basis stop so a 0.8-ATR print doesn't knock out a thesis that is still intact. On top of that I amend the neutral's demand for a stabilization signal before filling, because that is precisely the non-fill mechanism the 09-16 reflection indicts — the limit zone is retained, but with a five-session time/tape fallback so the desk does not repeat the error of gating adds below a rising baseline while Bollinger bandwidth compresses (8.88% versus 16.2% on 8/12) with a rising mid-band and lower band (330.96/311.02 on 9/24 → 331.90/317.17 on 10/2) — a coiling spring on a rising baseline is a configuration to be long ahead of, in size, not absent from.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE IT. Upgrade toward Buy on a daily close above 335.30 with volume above 42.2M followed by a held retest of 333–334, or on an FQ4 print with gross margin ≥49.5%, inventory converting rather than writing down, and the intangible explained. Move to Underweight on: gross margin below ~49% on the Q4 report (validating margin normalization with opex growing 22.9% versus 16.4% revenue), finished-goods inventory rising while revenue growth decelerates, deferred revenue growth below total revenue growth for another quarter (8.8% vs 16.1% is a real backlog question the bull never answered), a volume reclaim of 335.30 that fails back below 331.90 the next session (confirming overhead supply), any sourced negative catalyst, or a close below 322.42.

STATED GAPS. No peer or historical multiple set exists in this run, so the ~38x TTM EPS / ~2.8% FCF yield claim cannot be tested. No forward guidance, no segment, product, geographic or unit split, so 50.1% gross-margin durability is unattributable on both sides. No explanation of the $25.4B net intangibles increase (+91%). No options chain or implied volatility, so the suggested protective structure cannot be priced — gap risk is managed by gross exposure alone. No portfolio context was supplied, so every size is a fraction of the caller's own standard AAPL allocation and must respect their single-name limits.

**Price Target**: 345.34

**Time Horizon**: 1–3 months, re-underwritten at the late-October FQ4 FY2026 print

REFLECTION:
The 5-day window returned +0.9% raw but −0.3% alpha versus SPY, so the directional call was roughly right in absolute terms yet failed to beat the benchmark — too short and too small a sample to validate a 1–3 month Overweight thesis or its 345.34 target. What the window does support is the entry-geometry caution: the limit zone at 330.60–331.90 was not dislocated, and nothing in the tape yet confirms the 335.30 volume reclaim that would justify Tranche 2, while the gap-risk and closing-basis stop reasoning remains untested. The concrete lesson is that a sub-1% five-day move against SPY is not evidence for or against the thesis, so the next review should defer judgment to the 335.30 reclaim or the FQ4 print rather than treating a three-tenths alpha miss as a signal.

[2026-10-01 | AAPL | Overweight | +3.1% | +1.8% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Overweight

**Executive Summary**: Overweight AAPL, but do not pay for the full overweight before the late-October 10-K. Keep the core; if the caller is below standard AAPL weight, add only half of the proposed first tranche (~0.12-0.20% of portfolio) after AAPL tests 322-324 and stabilizes above the 50 SMA/61.8% retracement, with a hard closing stop at 316.8 and a no-add/reduce warning on a >50M-share close below 322.18. Cap total exposure at roughly 110% of standard allocation pre-10-K, use a >50M-share close above 335.30 as an add-on trigger, and release later tranches only after the 10-K confirms gross margin at/above 48-49% with inventory converting and after a sustained break above 341.07. Target 345.34 over 1-3 months.

**Investment Thesis**: The direction belongs to the bull case; the timing and sizing belong to the bear and neutral cases. The aggressive analyst is right that AAPL is not a broken franchise and that the primary trend remains intact: 9M FY2026 revenue grew 16.1% to $364.4B, Q3 revenue grew 16.4%, gross profit grew 25.3%, operating income grew 26.6%, EPS grew 28.7%, and Q3 gross margin reached 50.06% while 9M gross margin expanded 225 bps to 49.07% even with R&D up 32.5%. Net cash rose $22.5B to $64.2B, term debt fell $8.3B, and price remains above a rising 50 SMA at 322.18 and 200 SMA at 288.86 with a widening golden cross. The pullback has come on 36.3M shares versus 70.0M on 9/10 and 86.6M on 9/18, which is more consistent with digestion than distribution. That evidence rules out Hold or Sell and supports owning AAPL.

But the conservative and neutral analysts win the execution argument. At 330.32, AAPL is below the 10 EMA at 333.70, VWMA at 335.30, and Bollinger mid-band at 331.62, MACD has crossed down, and the 331-336 shelf is overhead resistance. A blind 323.5 limit is only ~2% below spot and would buy while the short-term tape is still deteriorating; the 316.8 stop is 6.7 points from entry, less than one ATR of 7.25, and AAPL has already printed -8.58%/-7.36% on 2026-07-31, -6.12% on 6/25, and -5.0% on 2/12. Stops do not protect against gaps; size does. The 10-K is also a known binary event, the last filing was 2026-07-31, and the durability of the 50% gross-margin level is unproven against forward memory-cost pressure. Inventory is +94%, raw materials +260%, finished goods -4.1%, intangibles +91%, other noncurrent liabilities +32.5%, R&D +32.5%, and buybacks slowed 12%—items that could support the product-cycle thesis but are not yet proof of demand.

The neutral construction therefore governs: retain the Overweight bias but make the first tranche conditional and half-sized, requiring stabilization at 322-324 rather than catching a falling knife; treat a close below 322.18 on >50M shares as a warning to stop adding and consider reducing, keep 316.8 as the hard closing stop, cap pre-10-K exposure near 110% of standard rather than 125%, and hold the larger adds for the 10-K gross-margin/inventory gate and a sustained break above 341.07. This avoids both errors in the record: the repeated cost of under-owning AAPL inside an intact uptrend, and the flat-alpha outcome from sizing above benchmark into extended, unconfirmed price. Upgrade toward Buy on a 10-K with gross margin at/above 49.5%, inventory converting, buybacks re-accelerating, and a high-volume close above 341.07/345.34. Downgrade toward Hold/Underweight on a >50M-share close below 322.18, a close below 316.8, a 10-K gross margin below 48%, an inventory write-down, or deteriorating demand. Stated gaps: no sentiment report, no options chain or implied volatility, no segment/product/unit data, and no portfolio context, so all sizing must be scaled to the caller's own standard AAPL allocation.

**Price Target**: 345.34

**Time Horizon**: 1-3 months, re-underwritten at the late-October 10-K

REFLECTION:
The +1.8% five-day alpha supports the Overweight directional call, but the window is far too short to validate a 1–3 month thesis or the 345.34 target. It supports the bull-case claim that AAPL’s primary uptrend was intact and that under-owning was the larger risk, while leaving untested the 322–324 stabilization, 335.30 VWMA reclaim, and 10-K gross-margin/inventory gates that governed sizing. Next time, tie the review window to the stated catalyst and predefine a short-horizon check—such as holding 322.18 and closing above 335.30—so a five-day alpha print is not mistaken for validation of a staged, event-gated plan.

[2026-09-30 | AAPL | Hold | +1.1% | -0.8% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Hold

**Executive Summary**: Hold AAPL: maintain the existing position at 0.75x–1.00x standard weight and place no new money at 333.02, which sits below the 10-EMA (334.45) and VWMA (335.34) for a second session with MACD 4.72 under its 5.32 signal and a 339.50 spike-and-fade on 49.99M shares still unresolved. Hard-cap exposure at 1.00x standard weight until the late-October FQ4/FY2026 print — not the 1.25x originally contemplated — because ATR is rising (6.83→7.25) and AAPL has already gapped −7.36% on 132.5M shares on 31 July, so size, not a closing stop, is the only real gap control. Stage any adds in three equal, evidence-gated tranches: a half-size probe only on two consecutive daily closes above 335.34 with no close back below 331.35, then a daily close above 339.50 on ≥50M shares with a held retest of 335.34, and the final third only after FQ4 clears gross margin ≥49.5%, revenue growth ≥15%, sequential inventory decline, tax ≤18%, and 10-K clarity on the ~$13B intangible/liability and its amortization terms. Risk ladder is closing-basis only: a close below 328.35 halts adds and forces a mandatory review, a close below 322.09 cuts to 0.5x standard weight, and a close below 316.27 exits to token/zero; if the position is above 1.00x, trim to the cap or buy a put/collar spanning the print rather than abandoning the core.

**Investment Thesis**: All three risk seats, the Research Manager and the trader land on Hold for AAPL, and here that is convergence rather than a shrug — the disagreement is only about the add ladder and the pre-print cap, and the bullish and bearish legs are genuinely symmetric at 333.02.

What the bullish case wins, and nobody rebutted it with a number: AAPL is not a broken franchise and the primary trend is up. Close 333.02 sits above a rising 50-SMA at 322.09 and a rising 200-SMA at 288.60, 15.4% above the 200-SMA with the 50-SMA 11.6% above the 200-SMA and widening, and 31 consecutive closes above the 50-SMA. Fundamentals are accelerating, not decaying: 9M revenue +16.1%, FQ3 revenue +16.4%, FQ3 gross margin 50.06% (+357 bps), FQ3 EPS +28.7%, 9M FCF $110.2B, net cash $62.2B with debt down 14.6%, and buybacks re-accelerated to $25.1B in FQ3 from $12.3B in FQ2. The bear produced no realized deterioration — no margin compression, no revenue loss, no unit weakness. That is why neither Underweight nor Sell survives: the conservative seat's own framing is "AAPL is not broken," and it conceded the franchise and the trend outright.

What the bearish case wins, and the bull conceded it twice: the entry is bad and the cash-flow headline is flattered.
